tool.name: vardictcpp
tool.command:
#if $select_mode.mode == "paired" ln -s '$select_mode.normal' ./normal.bam && ln -s '$select_mode.normal.metadata.bam_index' ./normal.bam.bai && #end if ln -s '$select_mode.tumor' ./tumor.bam && ln -s '$select_mode.tumor.metadata.bam_index' ./tumor.bam.bai &&
## vardictcpp (htslib) builds the .fai itself when it is missing, so no samtools is needed #if $reference_source.reference_source_selector == "history": ln -s '$reference_source.ref_file' ./ref.fa && #else if $reference_source.reference_source_selector == "cached" ln -s '$reference_source.ref_file.fields.path' ./ref.fa && ln -s '${reference_source.ref_file.fields.path}.fai' ./ref.fa.fai && #end if
## build the calling regions in plain shell (no python / awk needed) #set $rtype = str($region_source.region_type) #if $rtype == "genome" ## whole reference: one region per contig, read from the FASTA headers (optionally ## restricted to a chromosome list). vardictcpp clamps the end to each contig length and ## --chunk (below) tiles long contigs into windows so memory stays bounded. #if $region_source.interval_file: grep '^>' ./ref.fa | sed 's/^>//; s/[[:space:]].*//' | grep -Fx -f '$region_source.interval_file' | while read -r c; do printf '%s\t0\t999999999\t%s\n' "\$c" "\$c"; done > ./regions.bed && #else grep '^>' ./ref.fa | sed 's/^>//; s/[[:space:]].*//' | while read -r c; do printf '%s\t0\t999999999\t%s\n' "\$c" "\$c"; done > ./regions.bed && #end if #else if $rtype == "bed" ## normalise the user BED to a 4-column tab BED (vardictcpp needs column 4 for -g 4); ## comment / track / browser lines are dropped and the name defaults to the chromosome. ## To call a whole collection of BAMs each against its matching BED, map the tumor BAM over ## a BAM collection and this BED over a BED collection and Galaxy pairs them by element id. while read -r c s e n _; do [ -n "\$c" ] || continue; case "\$c" in '#'*|track*|browser*) continue;; esac; [ -n "\$e" ] || continue; printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "\$c" "\$s" "\$e" "\${n:-\$c}"; done < '$region_source.bed_file' > ./regions.bed && #else if $rtype == "text" ## typed regions arrive via a config file (never on the command line); each line becomes a ## 4-column tab BED, the name column defaulting to the chromosome. while read -r c s e n _; do [ -n "\$c" ] || continue; case "\$c" in '#'*) continue;; esac; printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "\$c" "\$s" "\$e" "\${n:-\$c}"; done < '$regions_input' > ./regions.bed && #end if
## vardictcpp only. --vcf writes VCF natively (in-C++ strand-bias Fisher test + var2vcf); no R / Perl. vardictcpp #if $select_mode.mode == "paired" -b "./tumor.bam|./normal.bam" -N 'Tumor|Normal' #else -b "./tumor.bam" -N 'Sample' #end if -G ./ref.fa -th \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1} --vcf #if $select_mode.mode == "single" --noend #end if #if $rtype == "genome" ## the per-contig regions span whole contigs; tile them into windows internally --chunk 1000000 #end if
-f '$advancedsettings.f' -k '$advancedsettings.k' -r '$advancedsettings.r' -B '$advancedsettings.B' -q '$advancedsettings.q' -X '$advancedsettings.X' -P '$advancedsettings.P' -o '$advancedsettings.o' -O '$advancedsettings.O' -x '$advancedsettings.x' -V '$advancedsettings.V' -m '$advancedsettings.m' -I '$advancedsettings.I' -L '$advancedsettings.L' -mfreq '$advancedsettings.mfreq' -nmfreq '$advancedsettings.nmfreq' $advancedsettings.t
#if $rtype == "single" ## single region of interest; -R takes coordinates directly (no BED / column flags) -R '$region_source.region' #else ## zero-based region BED (whole reference, user BED, or user-defined regions) -z -c 1 -S 2 -E 3 -g 4 ./regions.bed #end if
> '$variants'

Minimum number of reads for determining strand bias
Minimum phred score for a base to be considered a good call
Maximum number of extended bases after an indel to look for mismatches
Maximum average read position for a variant to be considered
Extend each region by N bases upstream and downstream
param.help: Pads every BED / -R region on both ends (e.g. 1000 = +/- 1 kb), so reads flanking the target are included. Default 0 = no extension.

param.label: Maximum variant allele fraction allowed in the matched normal
param.help: Somatic mode only: a candidate above this VAF in the normal is treated as germline/LOH rather than somatic.

param.label: Maximum mismatches before a read is discarded
param.help: Reads with more than this many mismatches (indel length not counted) are ignored.

param.label: Indel size (breakpoint search window for large indels)
Variant frequency threshold for monomer microsatellite (MSI) regions
Variant frequency threshold for non-monomer microsatellite (MSI) regions

tool.help:
vardictcpp ==========
**vardictcpp** is a standalone C++/htslib reimplementation of VarDict. It produces output byte-for-byte identical to VarDict-Java 1.8.3 at a fraction of the runtime and memory, in single-sample and paired (tumor/normal) modes.
The ``--vcf`` option makes vardictcpp compute the strand-bias Fisher test and write VCF natively in C++ (a direct port of VarDict's ``teststrandbias.R`` / ``testsomatic.R`` and ``var2vcf_valid.pl`` / ``var2vcf_paired.pl``), so the output is standard **VCF**:
- single-sample mode: one sample column (var2vcf_valid semantics), - paired mode: tumor and normal sample columns with somatic STATUS (var2vcf_paired semantics).
**Memory note:** VarDict holds all per-position data for the region it is processing in memory at once. Restrict calling to your actual targets (a BED file or typed regions) to keep memory low; calling whole chromosomes (or a whole-chromosome ``-R``) can use a very large amount of RAM.
Upstream: https://github.com/MHH-Bioinformatics-Hematology/vardictcpp
